features.headline: Breaking down the Players Era 8 Houston-Kansas championship game
features.desc: Houston was crowned the Players Era 8 champions Thursday night. How did it pull off the win?
body: The Players Era 8 championship in Las Vegas on Thursday was an all-Big 12 affair won by No. 8 Houston — which took down Rutgers and No. 1 Florida, on its way to the championship game.

Houston's opponent No. 11 Kansas, which cruised by UNLV in the first round but barely slid by West Virginia in the semifinals, cut its once 24-point deficit in the championship game to four, but the Jayhawks never took the lead.
Houston's 92-83 win over Kansas gives the Cougars two wins against top-15 teams already this season.
ESPN college basketball writers Jeff Borzello and Myron Medcalf have been following every game of this tournament. Borzello gives his biggest takeaway from Houston's championship run below.
How Houston won: If Kelvin Sampson wanted to show a potential recruit what Houston basketball looks like, he just needs to show them a video of the Cougars' first half Thursday night.

It was everything they pride themselves on, from dominating the offensive glass to forcing turnovers and overwhelming teams with their physicality on defense. And it was combined with fluid half-court offense and balanced scoring.
They took a 20-point lead into the break and led by as many as 23 points early in the second half.
The second half was a different story, as Kansas cut Houston's lead all the way down to four. And Sampson needed further heroics from Players Era 8 MVP Dedan Thomas Jr. to seal the win.

Thomas, who scored 30 points in the semifinals win over Florida, struggled with his shot for much of Thursday's game, but he scored back-to-back baskets and assisted Delrecco Gillespie on three straight possessions after Kansas trimmed the lead.

features.headline: Which player has the most career points in NHL history?
features.desc: Wayne Gretzky leads the list of NHL players with the most career points. Check out other top performers now.
body: Wayne Gretzky owns a laundry list of NHL records, including the mark for the most career points.
A player earns a point by either scoring a goal or getting an assist, which is credited to up to two players who pass the puck toward a teammate who scores.
Gretzky's 894 career goals plus his 1,963 career assists give him a grand total of 2,857 points over his illustrious 20-year career. That's nearly 1,000 more than any other player.

features.headline: 2026-27 MLB free agency, trade grades: Offseason analysis
features.desc: We've got you covered with grades and analysis on every winter signing and big offseason trade.
body: The 2026-27 MLB offseason is officially here, and we have you covered with grades and analysis for every major signing and trade as this winter — which is expected to include a labor stoppage — unfolds.
Whether it's a franchise-changing free agent signing or an unexpected blockbuster trade, we'll weigh in with what it all means for next season and beyond.

ESPN MLB experts Bradford Doolittle and David Schoenfield will evaluate each move as it happens, so follow along here, as this story will continue to be updated. Check back in for all the most recent analysis.
Colorado Rockies get: RHP Davis Martin RHP Luis Castillo
Chicago White Sox get: LHP Sean Sullivan C Douglas Veliz
The White Sox appear to be spending proverbial money to spend proverbial money.

That is to say, they are moving past the Castillo mistake from the last trade deadline — one whose ramifications were primarily monetary — and to do it, they are folding in a legitimate starter in Martin — a pitcher who, for the first few weeks of the 2026 season, looked like a Cy Young candidate.
They aren't spending actual money but are rearranging resources in hopes of spending money in a more productive way.

That's just reality, not an attempt to overhype Martin, whose season came unraveled the deeper we got into the calendar and who was ultimately not in position to help Chicago's staff once it reached the postseason.

Still, he put up more than 140 innings in each of the past two seasons with a 104 ERA+ during the pre-arbitration phase of his service time window. He was a valuable player for Chicago and therefore is now that for Colorado.

features.headline: C.J. Stroud, defense star as Texans get critical win over Colts on TNF
features.desc: C.J. Stroud and a swarming defense helped Houston beat Indy on 'Thursday Night Football.'
body: HOUSTON — The game was competitive for only the first quarter. After the Houston Texans went up 14-3 in the second quarter, they cruised to a 26-3 win against the Indianapolis Colts on "Thursday Night Football."

It was a complementary effort as Houston's offense scored 24 points, the defense notched a safety and special teams made plays, including a blocked field goal. It was the type of outing coach DeMeco Ryans had been yearning for all season.
Winning this matchup was a nonnegotiable for the Texans, who improved to 4-6. They couldn't afford to lose another winnable game.

Houston is fighting for its playoff life after losing last week to the Cleveland Browns in shocking fashion, blowing a 17-0 lead. But the Texans shook off the demoralizing loss and handled their business against Indianapolis.
Here are the most important things to know for both teams:

What to make of the QB performance: Quarterback C.J. Stroud got back on track after a shaky Week 10 loss against the Browns. Stroud looked in control outside of a couple of plays that resulted in an interception and a near interception. He finished the night with 194 yards and three touchdowns.

This is Stroud's third straight game with at least three touchdowns. And he has notched at least three scores through the air in four of his past five games. The Week 12 game presents a great opportunity for Stroud to continue his hot streak as Houston faces a struggling Ravens squad.
Trend to watch: Running back David Montgomery played how Houston hoped its major offseason acquisition would in his first game back since he hurt his groin in Week 4.
